verses.text: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his whole army and surrounded Jerusalem.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the city wall was broken through.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came in and sat at the Middle Gate: Nergal Sharezer, Samgar Nebo, Sarsechim the chief official, Nergal Sharezer the chief adviser, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they ran away. They left the city at night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Jordan Valley.

But the Babylonian army chased them and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where the king passed sentence on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
The Babylonians burned down the king's palace and the people's houses, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took into exile in Babylon the people who were left in the city, along with those who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left behind in the land of Judah some of the poorest people, who owned nothing. At that time he gave them vineyards and fields.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard:
"Take him and look after him. Do not harm him in any way. Do for him whatever he asks."
So Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, Nebushazban the chief official, Nergal Sharezer the chief adviser, and all the other officers of the king of Babylon
sent for Jeremiah and had him brought out of the courtyard of the guard. They put him in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him home. So Jeremiah stayed among the people.
While Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard, the LORD's message had come to him:

"Go and tell Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am going to carry out my words against this city, bringing disaster and not good. You will see it happen on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, says the LORD. You will not be handed over to the men you are afraid of.
I will certainly save you. You will not die by the sword. You will escape with your life, because you trusted in me, says the LORD.'"
